md_docs_2audio-channels(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2audio-channels(3)

NAME

md_docs_2audio-channels - Audio channels

All call encoders and decoders use stereo Opus. Speech uses centered input at 32 kbit/s; stereo microphones and media use 128 kbit/s. Internal PCM is interleaved stereo at 48 kHz, independent of device layouts and rates. PCM counts include both channels; codec frame durations are measured per channel.

Microphones

Use --list-microphones to choose a device. A multichannel device can still be used for mono speech. The device opener tries supported layouts and routes the selected input before resampling, echo cancellation, and microphone enhancement. 

# Stereo microphone, or the first pair on an audio interface
ascii-chat client --microphone-index 2 --microphone-channels 2
# A single microphone connected to input 3 (indices start at zero)
ascii-chat client --microphone-index 2 --microphone-channel 2
# Interface inputs 3 and 4 as a stereo pair
ascii-chat client --microphone-index 2 --microphone-channel 2 --microphone-channels 2
# Explicitly average all available inputs to centered mono
ascii-chat client --microphone-index 2 --microphone-channel -1

The same options apply to mirror and discovery modes and have corresponding ASCII_CHAT_MICROPHONE_CHANNEL and ASCII_CHAT_MICROPHONE_CHANNELS environment variables. The default selects input zero as mono speech. A microphone array's physical channels are not automatically treated as a stereo pair. Prefer its processed speech endpoint when available. Invalid selected pairs fail before opening a stream.

The browser device dialog offers Mono speech, Stereo pair, and a first input number starting at one. Browser support for exposing individual interface inputs varies. A browser-provided single channel stays centered. Browser AEC runs on microphone capture; shared C/WASM enhancement processes the microphone before stereo screen/media audio is mixed in.

Playback and media

  • Mono microphones are centered in both playback channels. Stereo sources retain their left/right separation through resampling, mix-minus, encoding, and recording.
  • Mono-only speaker devices receive a downmix. Multichannel outputs use the first stereo pair and silence the other outputs.
  • Clients advertise stereo support with AUDIO_CAP_STEREO. Call encoders and decoders default to two channels, and servers always send stereo output. There is no legacy-peer mono fallback.
  • Speech filters maintain independent channel state. Stereo gain control, compression, and gating use a shared detector to preserve channel balance.
  • Recordings retain stereo. Waveform/FFT displays downmix only their analysis copy.

Hardware-free validation

tests/unit/audio/stereo_test.c uses generated signals to check routing, resampling across callback boundaries, stereo codec defaults and explicit mono downmixing, stereo dynamics, jitter frame alignment, mix-minus, AEC buffer sizing, and recording timestamps. tests/contracts/audio/device_test.c simulates the PortAudio boundary while running the production callbacks and worker, including stereo-only microphones, mono speakers, and four-channel interface routing. Browser worklet tests generate independent microphone and media inputs.

tests/python/integration/stereo/test_audio_channels.py generates different tones in each channel and checks a real client/server call, including the received stereo WAV. Pass --artifacts-dir DIRECTORY to retain its logs and audio. The Chromium proof at web/web/tests/wasm/stereo-audio.mjs runs the real worklet, worker, C/WASM DSP, and Opus codec with generated microphone and media tracks. Run it against a local Vite server after rebuilding the WASM artifacts.

tests/audio/probe_aec3_echo.py LIBRARY --stereo checks independent playback channels, delayed synthetic echoes, and near-end speech while echo is present. The default invocation retains the mono regression.

These checks do not require a stereo microphone. Physical driver behavior and speaker-to-microphone acoustics still need hardware validation.
